entities.summary: Hasdrubal Gisco, a Carthaginian general, played a pivotal role in the Second Punic War, specifically in Iberia (Hispania) and North Africa. As the son of Gersakkun, a prominent Carthaginian, Hasdrubal Gisco was groomed for leadership from an early age. His military prowess and strategic thinking were instrumental in the Carthaginian victory at the Battle of Ilipa in 206 BCE, which gave the Carthaginians control of the Iberian Peninsula. However, his failure to capture the city of Saguntum in 219 BCE marked a turning point in the war, as it led to the Roman declaration of war against Carthage. Hasdrubal Gisco's legacy extends beyond his military campaigns, as he was also a skilled diplomat and administrator who played a key role in the development of Carthage's governance and economy. Despite his significance, Hasdrubal Gisco's life and achievements remain somewhat overshadowed by those of his more famous contemporaries, such as Hannibal. Nevertheless, his contributions to the Second Punic War and the history of the Mediterranean world continue to be studied and debated by historians today.
